root.name: Latvian Gambit Accepted: Foltys-Leonhardt Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 f5 3. Nxe5 Qf6 4. Nc4

overview: After 3.Nxe5 Qf6 4.Nc4 White has taken the e5 pawn and retreated the knight, and Black plays ...fxe4 and aims at White's development while the queen on f6 pressures b2 and f2. White keeps the extra pawn by developing with Nc3, d3 or d4.

white_ideas.idea: Keep the extra pawn with Nc3, d3 and Be3
Finish development and exploit the loose Black king

black_ideas.idea: Open the f-file with ...fxe4 and develop with ...Nc6 and ...d5
Counterattack on b2 and the centre with the queen

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after ...fxe4 with the black king slightly exposed

character.notes: Black plays for a lead in development and queen activity after giving the e-pawn.

gambit.notes: Black gave the e5 pawn and recoups only if White errs; White can keep it by simple development.

soundness.notes: White keeps a clean extra pawn if he consolidates, so the line is regarded as inferior for Black.

structure.notes: Pawns come off in the centre and files open early.

approach.notes: Black plays a rare countergambit that strong players seldom choose.

level.notes: White needs a handful of tactical responses.

character.reason: Black attacks at once with queen and pawn breaks while the king is exposed, so one slip decides the game.

gambit.reason: Black has lost the e5 pawn and White can hold on to it.

soundness.reason: Latvian Gambit lines are considered unsound by strong players.

structure.reason: The e- and f-files open quickly and the play is piece against piece.

level.reason: A dubious line is never Beginner, and only a limited amount of theory is needed.

plans.reason: Black tries to use development and queen play to make up for the pawn.
